headline: Southeast Asian countries are caught between competing US and Chinese AI blocs and fear being forced to choose sides, Nikkei Asia reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: only the opening paragraph could be read, so the claim and its detail are unverified.
importance_line: Governments and companies in Southeast Asia that buy AI chips, cloud services and models from both the US and China could come under pressure to pick one supplier, but which countries and which terms are involved is not known.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Southeast Asian countries are caught in the growing AI rivalry between the US and China, with many trying to keep ties with both while concern grows that they could be forced to choose sides, with consequences for business in the region.
notes: Only the standfirst and first paragraph were readable (subscription wall); no other outlet found for the same story, so the entry is headline-level.
